prsNoFiles: The pull request changes no files
prsCheckedOut: Checked out in {dir}: right-click a file to open it
prsDraftReview: {count, plural, =0 {Your review, no comments yet} one {Your review, # comment} other {Your review, # comments}}
prsDiscardDetail: Its comments and summary are deleted. Nothing was posted to GitHub.
prsStartDraftTip: Start a draft review without an agent. Add comments here, or with kero pr comment.
prsDraftHint: Agents add comments with kero pr comment --pr {number}.
prsDraftOld: The pull request changed after the review began. The comments stay on the older commit.
prsGuideEmptyDetail: An agent can write a tour of this pull request: its changes in reading order, each stop on the lines worth reading, with a note. The guide stays in Kero; nothing of it goes to GitHub.
prsGuideHint: Agents write guides with kero pr guide stop --pr {number}.
prsGuideWriting: An agent is writing the guide. Its stops show here as it adds them.
prsGuideStale: The pull request changed after the guide was written. Its lines may have moved.
prsGuideStops: {count, plural, =0 {Guide, no stops yet} one {Guide, # stop} other {Guide, # stops}}
prsGuideMoreLines: {count, plural, one {# more line in the full diff} other {# more lines in the full diff}}
prsGuideNoFile: The pull request doesn't change this file anymore.
prsGuideEnd: That's the tour. Your review is below.
prsGuideDiscardDetail: Its summary and stops go. Your draft review stays.
prsGuideStarted: Writing a guide of #{number} in the background. The Guide tab shows its stops as they come.
prsPostDetail: {count, plural, =0 {The review has no comments on lines. Everyone with access to the pull request sees it.} one {The review and its # comment go to GitHub as one review. Everyone with access to the pull request sees them.} other {The review and its # comments go to GitHub as one review. Everyone with access to the pull request sees them.}}
setPRNotifyDetail: New pull requests that ask for your review, or every new one someone else opens. Uses the GitHub CLI.
historyWorktreeInUse: Close the sessions that use this worktree first: {names}
historyWorktreeRemoveDirty: {count, plural, one {# changed file} other {# changed files}} in {path} will be lost. The branch stays, with its commits.
historyWorktreeRemoveUnpushed: {count, plural, one {# commit of {branch} isn't} other {# commits of {branch} aren't}} on a remote. Removing the worktree deletes its folder, and the branch keeps the commits. Push the branch to keep a copy on the remote.
historyWorktreeRemoveSafe: This deletes the folder {path}. The branch {branch} stays. It's pushed or merged, so you can also remove it without losing commits.
historyWorktreeRemoveBranchDetail: This deletes the folder {path} and the branch {branch}. Git deletes the branch only if it's merged.
historyViewNoneDetail: Open a commit in History, and click one of its files.
gitPickOlder: {count, plural, one {Show # branch older than {weeks} weeks} other {Show # branches older than {weeks} weeks}}
historyNotListed: That commit isn't in the listed history.
setBranchMaxAgeDetail: Hidden in the branch switcher until a search finds them.
setBranchMaxAgeWeeks: {count, plural, one {Older than # week} other {Older than # weeks}}
prsMergeBehind: Behind {base}: update the branch, or merge as it is if the repository allows.
prsMergeBlocked: Waiting on required reviews or checks.
prsMergeUnstable: Some checks failed, which the repository doesn't require.
prsMergeUnknown: GitHub is still checking whether it merges.
prsMergeConflicts: Conflicts with {base}: resolve them before merging.
prsMergeDraft: A draft: mark it ready for review to merge it.
prsMergeNoAccess: You can't merge pull requests of this repository.
prsAutoMergeOn: Merges by {method} once its requirements are met.
prsCloseDetail: It stays on GitHub, closed, with its branch, and you can reopen it.
prsRevertDetail: GitHub opens a new pull request into {base} that undoes this one's changes, for you to merge.
prsDeleteBranchDetail: This deletes the pull request's branch on GitHub, unless it has commits the pull request hasn't. Your local branches stay.
prsApproveRuns: {count, plural, =0 {Approve Runs} one {Approve # Run} other {Approve # Runs}}
prsApproveDetail: They run the fork's code with the repository's workflows. Look at its changes first.
prsRunsWaiting: {count, plural, one {A workflow run waits on your approval.} other {# workflow runs wait on your approval.}}
prsDoneAutoMerge: #{number} merges once its requirements are met
prsDoneApproved: {count, plural, =0 {No runs were waiting} one {Approved # run} other {Approved # runs}}
prsSetupMergeHint: How Merge merges this repository's pull requests. GitHub's is the first the repository allows of squash, merge commit and rebase.
setWorktreeCleanupNote: Only worktrees Kero made are removed. Kero never removes one a session works in, or one with uncommitted changes, untracked files, or ignored files that a build can’t make again, such as .env. Branches with commits of their own stay.
setWorktreeCleanupOnDetail: As Kero starts and every hour, when any rule below matches. Off by default.
setWorktreeCleanupInactiveDetail: No commit, checkout, or session in the worktree for this long.
setWorktreeCleanupMergedDetail: Its branch’s pull request on GitHub merged, at the commit the worktree is on.
setWorktreeCleanupUnchangedDetail: Nothing on its branch beyond the default branch.
setWorktreeCleanupClosedDetail: No session works in it anymore.
setWorktreeCleanupProjectDetail: A project of this computer can follow the rules above, keep its worktrees, or have rules of its own.
setWorktreeCleanupNowDetail: Runs the cleanup on this computer at once, with the rules as they are.
setWorktreeCleanupNoKerod: Kero isn’t connected to its background service.
setWorktreeCleanupSome: {count, plural, one {Removed # worktree} other {Removed # worktrees}}; some couldn’t be removed: {failed}
prLinkLink: Link to this session, which then wakes its agent when the checks fail
prLinkLinked: Linked to this session, which wakes its agent when the checks fail. Click to unlink.
setPRWatchWakeDetail: When the pull request of a session's branch, or one you linked, fails its checks or can't merge for conflicts; with All, also when its checks pass and when comments come. Uses the GitHub CLI.
sidebarOrchestratorTip: Orchestrator: it plans the work and follows the sessions under it
newSessionOrchestratorDetail: An agent that plans the work, starts sessions for it and follows them, and tells you how it goes. Kero reports to it what its sessions do.
newSessionGoalPlaceholder: What should it get done? Optional: it asks you otherwise.
confirmCloseOrchestratorDetail: It started {count} sessions. Close them too, or keep them as sessions of their own. A session in a worktree of its own keeps it.
setOrchestratorsDetail: An orchestrator plans the work and starts sessions for it, with kero new; Kero reports to it what they do.
setOrchestratorMaxDetail: How many of an orchestrator's sessions may run at the same time: past it, kero new refuses another.
setOrchestratorPromptDetail: The first message an orchestrator's agent gets. {goal} in it is the orchestrator's goal, {agent} the default agent.
setNotifyChildrenDetail: Notify of the sessions an orchestrator started, too. Off, they show in the sidebar alone, and only the orchestrator notifies: it hears of them itself.
amaAbout: Kero's helper agent, after amagaeru, the Japanese tree frog: it starts and manages your sessions for you
setAmaDetail: Ama, after amagaeru, the Japanese tree frog, is Kero's helper agent: open it from the frog at the bottom of the sidebar, and ask it to start, find or close sessions, worktrees and projects. It runs kero do, kero focus and kero browser without Remote Control.
setAmaAgentDetail: The agent command Ama runs, from its next chat on
setAmaInstructionsDetail: {file}: Ama reads it before Kero's own instructions, which Kero rewrites as it updates; Kero never changes this file
